name: radical
label: Radical — read the weakness and test the reply

states.label: Find the tactical idea
states.description: Read the board and choose the first theorem with a concrete chess cue. If none fits, try a forcing check or capture and read the resulting board. A failed theorem does not silently switch to a different plan.

predicates.label: If no candidate remains, attack the queen safely and test the reply

states.label: Read the board after a forcing move
states.description: After a forcing move, look again for a clear tactical idea. Examine every legal check evasion; otherwise examine the listed checks and recaptures, including a safe capture of our queen. If no theorem is visible when we can move, abandon this candidate.

predicates.label: If no candidate remains, attack the queen safely and test the reply

states.label: Force the alignment
states.description: Clear an aligned obstruction with check or check through the king to a piece behind it, then collect the aligned or loose target, renewing forcing exchanges when needed.

states.label: Deflect the defender
states.description: Draw a defender away by exchanging or offering a piece, then exploit the duty it abandons: a loose target, a fork square, a mating square, or a pawn blockade. Continue only when the resulting board supports the capture, checking fork, mate attack or promotion. Examine the listed recaptures and forcing counters, and settle the exchange before claiming its material goal. King acceptance and direct attacks on a passed pawn are explicit selective reply priorities.

states.label: Chase the sole defender
states.description: Attack the piece that alone protects an attacked target. If it moves away, collect the target. If it stays, a cheaper sacrifice or checking fork may force it to abandon its other duty; verify that exchange before collecting.

states.label: Threaten mate and win material
states.description: Use a mate threat to force a concession or win material. Prefer an available profitable queen capture and established forcing checks; keep the mating attack when a safe forcing continuation exists. Answer counterchecks, captures of the attacking piece, and the listed concrete mate defenses. After the threat wins material, settle the counters and protect any endangered collecting piece.

states.label: Break the king’s pawn shelter
states.description: Threaten mate against a pinned pawn beside the king and continue the attack against the listed safe checks, captures and mate defenses. The positional goal is a king forced away from its adjacent pawn shelter while we are not behind in material. This card certifies that exposed position, not a completed mate.

states.label: Repair the back rank with check
states.description: Before taking a loose prize, check in a way that also defends the enemy entry square. Then collect the prize without allowing mate in one.

states.label: Overload a pinned piece
states.description: Attack a pinned piece safely. If it receives another defender, threaten both it and a second loose target; otherwise collect it. A supported pin of the queen can serve the same purpose.

states.label: Save with a threat; harass the queen
states.description: Save an attacked piece, exchange its attacker, or create a double attack with a threat against the queen. Prefer a safe material gain before preparing another threat; consider a checking fork before a quiet double attack. Examine the listed captures of the attacker, safe queen escapes and forcing material counters; an attacked piece may also capture with check before it is lost. Collect the forked target and verify that the gain survives the immediate counterplay.

states.label: Check fork, collect, and protect
states.description: Check while attacking a second target, clearing a knight-fork square first if necessary. Examine the relevant legal evasions and collect the exposed piece safely. Challenge the gain with the listed checks, material-recovering captures and safe attacks, then protect the threatened collecting piece. A takeback that leaves the stated material goal intact need not extend the line.

predicates.label: If no plan move remains, collect from the improved position and test the gain

states.label: Check the material gain
states.description: Check whether the opponent can check or recover the material. Examine the listed forcing counters and finish the exchange, including available takebacks after a capturing promotion. When no relevant counter remains, inspect our loose pieces.

states.label: Protect our loose pieces
states.description: Test safe attacks on our loose pieces. Capture the attacker, add a defender, or move the attacked piece; prefer a useful counterthreat when escaping a cheaper attacker. Finish only when the stated immediate safety conditions hold.

states.label: Take a pawn with tactical protection
states.description: Take a pawn whose apparent defender is constrained by a tactical threat. Examine recaptures, checks, attacks on loose pieces and relevant developing attacks; use a checking skewer if the recapture opens one. Rescue endangered pieces while preserving the pawn gain. A queen exchange may instead leave a smaller but real material advantage: settle the captures and protect the surviving pieces before accepting that queenless ending.

states.label: Find an endgame idea
states.description: A knight against a bishop and a king-defended enemy pawn suggests checking away the defender and collecting the pawn. Other positions use the original ideas.

states.label: Check away a pawn defender
states.description: Check the king while attacking its pawn; examine every legal evasion, then collect the pawn. The provisional positional theorem is a gained pawn and an intact four-pawn chain against a bishop sharing the color of at least three of its own pawns, with the knight safe and forcing counters checked. This is a covering hypothesis, not a universal endgame proof.

states.label: Place the king with a rook or forcing queen check
states.description: With bishop control around an edge king, try a rook check or a safe queen check with one reply. Reread the resulting board immediately, test their evasions, and continue the visible threat.

states.label: Force the king and remove its blocks
states.description: Continue forcing checks and checking captures. Examine every legal evasion. When a block stops the check, take it with check or renew the check. When the material objective is reached, test that the gain survives.

states.label: Hold the passer and reach the locked wing
states.description: Only kings and two pawns each remain: one passed pawn each, and a locked pair at least three files away. Their passer is two moves from promotion and lies toward the locked wing. Move the king to attack and block it while guarding our passer. The provisional terminal requires our passer between the kings, their king attacking that guarded pawn, and the locked pair level with our king and passer. This is a specific geometric covering hypothesis for later independent endgame validation, not a general claim that any extra pawn wins. The locked pair must be off the edge file: rook-pawn versions admit draws and are excluded.

states.label: Advance and promote the passed pawn
states.description: In the endgame, a safe advance can put a passed pawn one step from promotion. Advance it, examine every legal opponent reply, and promote to a queen. Accept the existing mate certificates or a promotion that leaves a material advantage without an immediate mating, checking, capturing or safe counterattacking recovery. In a pure two-pawn race, advance an unreachable passer from earlier ranks and examine every legal reply. A clear promotion lead of two tempi is a provisional race covering certificate; a closer race continues to promotion. No universal endgame proof is claimed.

states.label: Take the piece and stop the passer
states.description: Below the material threshold, safely capture the last enemy piece with a knight. Examine every legal reply, then place the safe knight to control the sole passed pawn’s promotion. The provisional positional certificate also requires a material advantage, our nearer king, and no immediate enemy check or capture.

states.label: Attack a pawn or create a runner
states.description: In a pawn ending, collect a pawn or create a runner. Answer a check by first trying a safe or defended capture of the checker. A clear runner with two tempi in hand covers quiet replies; test their checks. Otherwise test every legal reply, and reread the same pawn and race facts after collecting. Accept only the explicit pawn-gain and race certificates below; these retain the prior provisional endgame hypotheses.

states.label: Secure the extra pawn in a minor-piece ending
states.description: Below the material threshold, a bishop versus knight exchange leaves an extra pawn. Answer checks, prefer a king response defending an attacked pawn, and collect safe captures. The provisional terminal records positive gained material with no immediate mate or safe check/capture; it does not claim every admitted ending is a forced win.

proof.scope: Selective human tactical investigation. Each current card chooses moves, replies and continuations from chess predicates. Some cards examine every legal check evasion; others explicitly prioritize a king capture, safe forcing counters, queen escapes or concrete mate defenses. Claims cover those generated replies and the stated material or positional goal.
proof.quiet_definition: Completion uses the current card's explicit board conditions. A material goal may survive an available takeback; pawn-gain, queenless-advantage, exposed-king and repaired-piece goals have their own conditions. The absence of a generated reply does not assert that all legal moves are equivalent.

positional_objectives.BREAK_KING_SHELTER: From equal material, expose the opposing king without falling behind in material. This proves the declared board transformation only; it does not by itself prove forced mate or an eventual material win.
